newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia nickel held up by floods at port - Norilsk.
newsitem.headline: Russia nickel held up by floods at port - Norilsk.

text.p: Russian nickel exports are being delayed by flooding at the Arctic port of Dudinka, but delays should only last a few weeks and are not unusual for this time of year, a RAO Norilsky Nikel spokesman said Tuesday.
"There is big flooding at the port," said Anatoly Komrakov, a Moscow-based Norilsk spokesman. "Usually the water rises by about five metres at the port, but now it is up eight metres."
He was responding to talk on the European physical nickel market that there had been early flooding at Dudinka, reducing Russian supplies to the West.
Komrakov said the delays should be expected.

"Everyone knows very well -- buyers and traders -- that for several weeks during this period of the year exports can be interrupted," he said. "It is what we expected, and really nothing extraordinary."
Dudinka is the export outlet for base metals from Russia's dominant nickel producer, Norilsk.

Last week Komrakov said production at the group's flagship metals plant had risen 11 percent during the first quarter of the year over the same year-ago period. "This is in accordance with what we planned earlier," he said on Tuesday.
The combine accounts for the bulk of the Norilsk group's nickel production. The group produced 177,185 tonnes of nickel in 1996, down slightly from 180,100 tonnes in 1995.
Norilsk said in February it was aiming to boost output by around 20 percent in the short to medium term.
